answer: My grandmother ran a small orchard at the edge of town, and every autumn she sold apples by the roadside with a tin box for the money. She never locked it. When I asked why, she laughed and said an unlocked box is not a puzzle to solve but a promise to keep - the whole village understood that cipher without being taught. Years later I found one of her old coins in a drawer, polished smooth, with a pearl pressed into the metal where the mint mark used to be. Trust, she proved, ages better than gold.
